From: Alex Moretti <amoretti@medcorehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA/order form: scope question — audit window and pen test

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our procurement and security teams flagged two items that need clearer language before we can move to signature:

1) Audit window / inspection rights — we need the contract to clarify whether inspection is limited to a 5-business-day window per quarter or if you intend rolling access. Our SOC 2 compliance team prefers defined windows for planning resources.

2) Pen test access — they want explicit timing, notice period, and whether Redwood will provide staging credentials or if MedCore should perform externally (and what evidence we get back).

Can you share the security exhibit redline you'd like to push (or a short summary of the changes you propose around evidence cadence + staging access)? We want to align that with our procurement timeline — they aim to complete legal redlines by Friday (4/28).

Appreciate any quick clarifications. If it helps, I can set a 20-min sync for Thurs.

Best,
Alex
Head of IT Risk
MedCore Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/order form: scope question — audit window and pen test

Alex — thanks for the clear notes and the timeline. High level summary of what we propose (see attached PDFs for the redline + cadence workbook):

- Audit windows: We propose defined quarterly inspection windows (one 5-business-day window per quarter, scheduled at least 30 days in advance) with an optional rolling 2-business-day hot-window for critical investigations (requires written justification). This balances predictability with operational safety for multi-tenant infrastructure.

- Pen test access: Redwood will accept third-party pen tests on a staging environment. We will provide ephemeral staging credentials and a dedicated support channel during the test window. Notice: 14 calendar days for standard tests; 30 calendar days for tests that require infra staging changes.

- Evidence cadence: monthly SOC 2 artifact snapshots (read-only), on-request logs (redacted where necessary) within 5 business days, and an "evidence sprint" deliverable after each pen-test with a summary report and sample telemetry for confirmed findings.

What we've attached: redwood_security_exhibit_v2.pdf (annotated MSA redline) and proposed_evidence_rhythm.xlsx (a week-by-week cadence suggestion that maps doc types to owners).

Next steps: Karthik — can you confirm the legal phrasing we should propose for the inspection clause? Marcus — can you confirm the ops process for issuing ephemeral staging creds and the retention window for the requested logs? Alex — if that aligns we can push a tracked redline back to your procurement team by end of day Thurs (4/28).

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Legal (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Alex / Laura — quick legal note and suggested redline language for the inspection and penetration testing sections. Trying to keep the customer's ask while protecting platform stability and other customers. Suggested insertion (replace current paragraph under "Inspection Rights" in Security Exhibit):

"Inspection Rights. Customer may request access to evidence and records necessary to validate Redwood's compliance with the Agreement. Such access shall be limited to one (1) scheduled inspection window of up to five (5) consecutive business days per calendar quarter, to be mutually agreed upon at least thirty (30) days prior to the start of the window. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may request up to two (2) shorter ad-hoc inspection windows of up to two (2) consecutive business days each, upon written justification and subject to Redwood's reasonable operational constraints. Redwood will not be required to disrupt production environments or perform exhaustive forensic activities during these ad-hoc windows."

Pen-test clause (summary):
- Third-party pen tests are permitted on a staging environment only; Customer must provide evidence of insurer/authorization and an agreed scope.
- Notice: 14 days for standard scope; 30 days where infra modifications are required.
- Redwood will provide ephemeral credentials and a single point of contact. Redwood reserves the right to terminate access that risks platform stability.

Privacy/confidentiality: insert a cross-reference to the Confidentiality Section limiting dissemination of evidence to named individuals. Also proposing that log extracts be redacted to remove data linked to other customers.

If that looks ok to you Alex, we'll produce a tracked-change version for procurement. Laura and Marcus — if you see any operational risk with the 5-day quarterly window or the 14-day notice, highlight now.

—Karthik
VP, Legal (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 28 Apr 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/order form: scope question — audit window and pen test

Thanks — quick ops confirmation from my side:

- Staging access: we can provision ephemeral staging credentials scoped to a single project/tenant. Credentials expire automatically after the window and we record the issuance metadata (requestor, IP, time range).
- Ephemeral creds timeline: we need a minimum of 3 business days to stand up a scoped staging environment (14/30-day notice still applies for full test planning).
- Logs and telemetry: we can provide redacted request logs, system logs, and tokenized traces for confirmed incidents. Retention: 90 days for detailed telemetry, 1 year for aggregate metrics.
- Evidence sprint: post-test we will provide a 5-business-day response with a summary report, remediation actions (if any), and a sample of telemetry packets for validated findings. Sensitive fields will be redacted; any PII relating to other customers will be removed.

Operational caveat: exhaustive, on-demand forensic pulls against production may require a formal SOW (to cover engineering costs). We'll include that language in the tracked redline.

Alex — happy to hop on the short sync Thurs if you want to walk the cadence with your security team; otherwise we can push the tracked redline by EOD Thurs so procurement has it for review.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
